intro: I’m Anand Grandhi. I work at the intersection of product strategy, business operations and applied AI.

I joined BYJU’S in 2015, before its flagship learning app launched, and helped build and scale its learning products during five years of rapid growth. At Amazon, I worked on product adoption, customer experience and operational transformation.
Today, through ARCHMATION, I apply that experience to intelligent workflows and complex business problems.

projects.title: Using AI to take a six-hour workflow down to 45 minutes
projects.problem: Publishing a single article meant researching, drafting, reviewing and moving information between multiple tools. The production process was consuming hours of skilled team time.
projects.discovery: Writing was only one part of the problem; coordination and repetitive handoffs were also consuming time.
projects.decision: Rather than simply introducing an AI writer, I designed a workflow around the entire production process.
projects.approach: I defined an AI-assisted research and content pipeline using structured inputs, automation and editorial review, connecting research, drafting and publishing.
projects.outcome: Reported production time fell from 6.5 hours to 45 minutes per article.
projects.assurance: Human editorial review remained part of the workflow. The time-saving figure is a reported project outcome.

projects.title: From Question of the Day to a daily learning habit
projects.problem: Daily engagement was declining: active users had fallen from approximately 50,000 to 35,000. The original Question of the Day offered a reason to open the app, but did not consistently connect that visit with meaningful progress.
projects.discovery: Behavioural and product data pointed to friction in getting started, difficulty choosing relevant activities and weak reasons to return. The opportunity was to reduce decision effort and connect short sessions with the next useful action.
projects.decision: I proposed Daily Digest: short personalised sessions combining behavioural nudges, habit formation, relevant practice and clear next actions, rather than another feed of content.
projects.approach: I defined the core journey and personalisation logic using activity, progress, weak areas and goals. I worked with product, UX, research, ML, engineering and content teams on the experience, notification strategy and iterative improvements.
projects.outcome: Previously reported DAU recovered from approximately 35,000 to 80,000+. Reported retention increased by 32% and session duration by 64%. These are observational product metrics, not controlled causal estimates.
projects.assurance: I monitored engagement and retention after launch and used the results to prioritise improvements. Leadership made final feature decisions.

projects.title: Designing intelligence for personalised counselling
projects.problem: Personalised university admissions counselling relies on evolving student context and institutional expertise accumulated over roughly a decade across documents, recordings and Airtable records.
projects.discovery: Counsellors need to retrieve relevant institutional knowledge, maintain a consistent student record and turn conversations into informed next steps, without repeatedly reconstructing context.
projects.decision: I defined three connected capabilities: Transcript Intelligence, Intelligent Counselor Workbook and Personalized Student Planning Engine.
projects.approach: During an approximately 40-day paid advisory engagement, I developed product strategy, workflow requirements, decision logic, evaluation requirements and implementation planning. The planning engine proposes feasible next steps based on goals, eligibility, prerequisites and time constraints.
projects.assurance: Source traceability, privacy, incomplete or contradictory information, feasible recommendations and counsellor approval were explicit product requirements.
projects.outcome: The advisory deliverables define an interconnected product architecture and implementation direction for Athena’s teams. Deployment and commercial impact are not claimed.

projects.title: AI transformation for an early-stage startup
projects.problem: A recruitment technology startup needed to make institutional knowledge easier to access, reduce repetitive coordination and establish a more systematic approach to early customer adoption.
projects.discovery: The opportunity was to create reusable AI capabilities across teams rather than disconnected prompts, with explicit ownership, approval and evidence requirements.
projects.decision: I structured the work around an intelligent knowledge base and employee assistant, an Agent Backbone for operations, an Agent Backbone for software development, and GrowthOS for acquisition.
projects.approach: I defined use cases, requirements, workflow logic, qualification rules and acceptance criteria. AI-assisted prototypes covered knowledge retrieval, requirements drafting, engineering planning and evidence-led prospect research.
projects.assurance: The common reliability approach included source grounding, deterministic validation, human approval and representative tests. Commercial acquisition and deployment outcomes are not established.
projects.outcome: Functional prototypes and product specifications demonstrated selected workflows, including planning, validation and approval. Broader production integration remained a separate engineering responsibility.

projects.title: Publishing faster without sacrificing editorial accuracy
projects.problem: Repeated reviews slowed the release of learning content and created avoidable coordination across subject experts and editorial teams.
projects.discovery: The process needed clearer quality criteria and fewer avoidable review loops, rather than simply asking teams to work faster.
projects.decision: I focused on standardising quality expectations and improving the review workflow.
projects.approach: I worked on editorial operating processes, review criteria and production coordination across teams.
projects.outcome: Reported publishing turnaround decreased by 40%, accuracy reached 98%, and review rounds fell from eight to three.
projects.assurance: Quality and turnaround were monitored together so speed would not become the only success measure.

projects.title: Building and scaling digital learning products
projects.problem: During BYJU’S rapid expansion from its flagship app launch, the product needed consistent learning experiences across subjects, grades and formats while coordinating multidisciplinary teams.
projects.discovery: Scaling required a shared structure for learning objectives, content specifications, interactive experiences and review—not simply increasing production volume.
projects.decision: I focused on knowledge architecture, guided learning journeys, interactive STEM and repeatable production processes.
projects.approach: I led and collaborated across subject experts, product, design, art, engineering and production teams. The work connected concept-level specifications to videos, assessments, games, simulations and guided experiences.
projects.outcome: The work supported the expansion of digital learning products and repeatable multidisciplinary delivery. The programme-scale outputs describe team contributions rather than individual production.
projects.assurance: Subject-matter validation, common specifications and coordinated quality reviews were foundational.
projects.context: Company context: BYJU’S launched its flagship learning app in 2015. By June 2020, it had reported more than 57 million registered users, 3.5 million paid subscribers and a reported $10.5 billion funding-round valuation. These historical company-level milestones provide context for the growth environment, not outcomes attributable to my work.

projects.title: Removing friction from the student doubt-resolution journey
projects.problem: Students encountering a difficult question needed a way to get help without losing momentum in their learning journey.
projects.discovery: Doubt resolution needed to be treated as a product experience, not simply a support activity.
projects.decision: I defined the core behaviour and user journey for doubt resolution, connecting help with the learning experience.
projects.approach: I contributed to the launch of doubt on chat and its integration with the help centre, working across product and operations.
projects.outcome: The service handled more than 50,000 queries in its first three months.
projects.assurance: The volume demonstrates usage, not a verified resolution-quality or satisfaction score.

projects.title: Helping teachers see where students were actually struggling
projects.problem: Assessment data could show which students scored poorly, but teachers also needed to understand what concepts and misconceptions were driving those scores.
projects.discovery: A raw score is less actionable than a view of concept-level gaps and cohort patterns.
projects.decision: I focused on translating student assessment and engagement data into instructional priorities.
projects.approach: I worked on teacher insight concepts using knowledge-graph mappings, assessment results and misconception patterns to support lesson preparation.
projects.outcome: The approach supported more targeted instructional planning. A quantified impact figure is not available here.
projects.assurance: The design relied on concept mappings and assessment evidence rather than unsupported inferences.

projects.title: Turning fragmented content into structured knowledge
projects.problem: Large learning libraries are difficult to personalise when content lacks a shared map of concepts and prerequisites.
projects.discovery: A structured representation of learning objectives can connect content, assessment, remediation and progression.
projects.decision: I focused on defining testable learning objectives and their relationships, including prerequisites and misconception mappings.
projects.approach: I worked on testable learning objectives, prerequisite and thematic relationships, and content tagging across curricula, connecting learning assets and assessments to a shared conceptual structure.
projects.outcome: The BYJU’S K–12 knowledge graph comprised an estimated 50,000–75,000 nodes across PCMB. These programme-scale structures supported content tagging, discovery and learning pathway design; related work continued at Amazon.
projects.assurance: Subject-matter expertise and content mapping were foundational to the approach.

projects.title: Scaling learning content without scaling complexity
projects.problem: A rapidly expanding digital learning platform needed consistent content across subjects, grades and formats, requiring coordination between subject experts, creative teams and production partners.
projects.discovery: The bottleneck was not simply the availability of subject expertise; it was the ability to translate that expertise into repeatable production workflows.
projects.decision: The focus was to standardise learning specifications, content handoffs and quality expectations across disciplines.
projects.approach: I contributed to product development and content production initiatives across learning assets, assessments and solutions, collaborating with multidisciplinary teams.
projects.outcome: Reported programme-library scale included 25,000+ animated videos, 3.5 million+ assessment assets and 100,000+ solutions. These describe wider programme scale, not assets personally produced.
projects.assurance: Subject-matter accuracy and consistent learning objectives were essential to the production approach.

projects.title: Turning passive video lessons into guided learning journeys
projects.problem: Watching a lesson does not necessarily reveal whether a learner has understood the material or is ready to progress.
projects.discovery: Learning experiences needed opportunities to practise, retrieve knowledge and check understanding within the journey.
projects.decision: I focused on guided learning journeys that combined explanations with questions, flashcards and checkpoints.
projects.approach: I worked on chemistry learning journeys for competitive exam preparation, defining the instructional sequence and interactive checkpoints.
projects.outcome: The work established a structured learning experience combining instruction and practice. Quantified adoption or learning improvement is not available here.
projects.assurance: The experience was grounded in subject-matter objectives and checkpoints rather than video completion alone.

projects.title: Simplifying internal operations with AI
projects.problem: Routine internal questions, scattered procedures and outstanding task follow-ups consume employee and manager attention.
projects.discovery: The opportunity is to improve access to approved information and task visibility without introducing another complex operating system.
projects.decision: I formulated three lightweight workflows: employee onboarding and training, searchable internal SOPs, and task visibility with reminders.
projects.approach: The design uses a shared training and SOP repository, a central task tracker for owners and due dates, and n8n to route reminders through WhatsApp and Gmail. WhatsApp is for notifications, not training or the authoritative record.
projects.assurance: Approved sources, escalation for unanswered questions, a single authoritative task record and human responsibility for completion and exceptions.
projects.outcome: The workflow design establishes a practical implementation direction using existing tools. Deployment, adoption and quantified savings are not asserted.

projects.title: Building a trustworthy AI workflow for customer acquisition
projects.problem: Early-stage growth teams need to research potential customers, qualify opportunities and coordinate follow-up without losing track of evidence or decisions.
projects.discovery: Automating activity alone is not enough: unverified claims and premature funnel-stage changes can create unreliable growth reporting.
projects.decision: I focused on separating account research, validation and qualification, with explicit rules for when an action or stage transition is allowed.
projects.approach: I explored a multi-agent workflow and an AI-assisted reference system for structured research, evidence-based qualification and controlled operations.
projects.outcome: A reference run demonstrated a citation rejection and correction loop. The prototype test suite and dry run demonstrated approval and evidence controls; commercial growth outcomes are not claimed.
projects.assurance: Human approval gates, deterministic checks and evidence-based stage transitions were central to the design.
